meta.primary_source: Ahn et al. 2011, 'Flavor network and the principles of food pairing', Scientific Reports 1:196. Co-occurrence data from global recipe databases (Epicurious, allrecipes, and others).
secondary_sources: Page & Dornenburg 2008, 'The Flavor Bible' — expert chef consensus pairings.
CSIRO Sensory and Flavour Science / Orana Foundation — Australian native ingredient culinary research.
Jock Zonfrillo & various Australian native food practitioners — native-to-contemporary crossover pairings.
meta.methodology: affinity_score normalized from recipe co-occurrence frequency and/or expert culinary consensus. 0.9+ = universal classic (thousands of recipes); 0.8 = strong established pairing; 0.65-0.75 = well-documented culinary use; 0.45-0.60 = emerging or modern gastronomy. ALL pairs are ingredient-level, not brand-level. Compound overlap with Cobber's aroma DB is noted per pair where it exists.
meta.note: Culinary affinities are DISTINCT from cocktail tradition scores. A high score means chefs use these together in food contexts — the host Claude decides whether it translates to a cocktail. Many pairs here have NO shared compound in Cobber's aroma DB (which is aroma-only); the pairing is validated by culinary empiricism, not compound analysis. When shared_compounds is mentioned in a note, the chemistry AND culinary tradition agree — strongest possible signal.
